lens: L1 skeptic (one input moves a shared value), checked against guard/snap. 22 of 23 instances are real; L1-23 is a list of guarded patterns, not a defect. All 15 finder tests fail on the snapshot for the reason they state. Corrections: (1) L1-1 is narrower for other payers and worse for the stray payer's own group than described: states.py already keeps the cross-payer flood in 'Can't be checked' (per-group MAX), but one adjustment-only 835 from Medicare KY put 610 claims ($143,356) into Work now on a copy of the live image with the snapshot's code. (2) Production and A/R are worse than stated, shown through the real read path: the correct newer A/R is superseded, and G8 lists answered claims as never answered. (3) Severity is lower for L1-6, L1-7 and L1-19. (4) L1-12 does not reach the worklist yet: selfcheck's hooks are not wired in the snapshot. (5) The source lint counts 60 sites, but about 15 are grouped, per-claim, per-file or display only, and it misses the Python-side extremes. My tests, scripts and aggregate results are in guard/L1/verify/ (10 tests fail for the stated reason, 4 controls pass). Real data was used only as copies (an in-memory copy, and a file copy deleted after use), and only aggregates are reported.

verdicts.status: confirmed; the snapshot partly guards the other payers (states.py), the stray payer's own group is not guarded; shapes (b) and (c) are not guarded
verdicts.why: Detector.run_ema_open_claims gates every payer's open claims with MAX/MIN(payment_date) (2514-2520), with the due day compared to the global newest date (2774-2777) and severity set by first <= newest+30 (2880). Reproduced. The finder missed a partial guard: states._cant_check reads group_last_835, the MAX per payer group (states.py 973-980, 2521-2542). So another payer's claims that a stray file lets through become 'Can't be checked' (next step: call), not 'Chase the payer'. The stray payer's own group goes to Work now. Nothing catches the one-day bundle (c) or the future date (b). The real hotfix-2 feed_date also bridges (c). The selfcheck 'vanished' rule would put back the items a future-dated file wipes, but it is not wired in the snapshot (it is in needs_G.md only).

verdicts.status: confirmed with items in an invented world (finder: high); on the live image one line cannot flip a tier
verdicts.why: No floor per NPI. Top = MAX of each NPI's usual Medicare amount, and the tier comes from the median ratio. A flip removes or moves rate-based items. Each tier is the median over the NPI's (year, code) pairs, so one line moves only one pair.
verdicts.evidence: guard/L1/verify/test_v_l1_tiers.py fails: the physician's 3 underpayment items ($49.50) vanish after one +10% line from a new NPI. probe_l1_7.py, with 4 more lines: 7 items, $109.50. Live provider_tiers: the 4 physicians have 12, 12, 12 and 3 pairs, so a flip needs higher lines in 7 of 12 pairs (2 of 3 for one physician). The finder's live figure injected one line per year and code. Payer rate baselines do have n >= 10 floors (detect.py 875-904).

verdicts.status: confirmed; the 're-saved' path is narrower, the CSV path is wider
verdicts.why: A status export is ranked by the workbook's dcterms:created. Excel, LibreOffice and openpyxl keep that stamp on a plain re-save. It moves only when an old export is rebuilt as a new workbook (copied into a new file, made by a script, downloaded from Google Sheets). A CSV has no stamp. ema_paid then ranks by file name, and M-D-YY names sort wrong ('Encounter 10-12-26.csv' < 'Encounter 9-14-26.csv'). run_ema_open_claims ranks a CSV by the newest date in any one row (2573-2581).
verdicts.evidence: The finder's test fails. openpyxl 3.1.5 load, delete a column, save: dcterms:created unchanged (checked in verify/). Code read: detect.py 762-775 and 2566-2616.

verdicts.status: confirmed, narrower path (finder: high); the impact (patient records to a wrong fax line) is high
verdicts.why: A first saved number gets auto_ok=1. number_hold lets an automatic send use it when the item has no earlier fax at that level. The daily run (_send_followups, from api.py 4872 and cli.py 465) sends next-level appeals, with the payer's decision attached, to the level_2 number, else the appeal number. So a first-saved level-2 number gets an automatic send that no person pressed. At level 1, retries and second requests go only to the number the item's last fax went to, and a person pressed that send.
verdicts.evidence: Code read: actions.py 89-120, fax.py 421-460 and 580-590, api.py 4395-4415 and 4593-4712, faxes.js 307.

detect.run_ema_open_claims gates claims still in EMA's print batch and never sent (REJECTED_PRE_PAYER 'unsent') on the remittance date (due > newest, about 2765-2777), though no 835 can answer a claim that was never sent. While the feed is stale they stay hidden: guard/L1/verify/test_v_l1_states.py::test_a_claim_never_sent_is_listed_by_todays_date_not_by_the_remittance_date fails with the feed stopped Sept 1 and passes with it current. On the live-image copy, 19 such claims ($4,884) appear only when a newer (even stray) 835 arrives.

Silent drop at detect.py 2777: claims dropped because the remittances do not reach their due day are counted nowhere. meta ema:unanswered_unseen counts only claims dropped later, in _ema_check_open_claims, so a future-dated file wipes the open items with n=0 recorded. Owner rules 1 and 3.

api._note_batch_since (api.py 3028-3038): MIN(service_date) over the open note items sets ModMed's export _since for every 'Build packets from EMA' batch. One item with a far-past service date widens every export. Low.

selfcheck._ar_balance uses MAX(as_of) FROM ema_ar (selfcheck.py 2024), and the self-audit check window uses MIN/MAX of ema_checks posted dates (2899): store-wide values from one row each. Not wired today. Low.

The class lint: about 15 of its 60 hits are not store-wide (grouped beyond its 400-character look-ahead: archive.py 1248, alerts.py 299, ema_ledger.py 1431/1437/1548/1573/1574; per-claim or per-file keys it does not recognise: detect.py 4098, ema_checks.py 1636, ema_reports.py 2920; display-only statistics: ema_ledger.py 544, cli.py 148/504, api.py 427-428, cloud.py 1200-1201), so it needs an allowlist from day one. It also misses extremes outside its 5 column names or outside SQL: Python max() in detect._ratio and _newest_fees, iter_ar's flush, coverage() and freshness(); MAX(month) in ema_checks.py 376; the CSV content rank at detect.py 2573; the ledger box bounds at ema_ledger.py 625; MIN(service_date) at api.py 3034.
